answer_text: I used a sliding window instead of a fixed counter to prevent burst traffic exactly at the minute boundary.
To handle thread safety, I could have used a Redis lock, but since this was for a single process I used threading.Lock.
I set the expiration to 60 seconds. For memory efficiency with lots of users, a sorted set in Redis would be better than an in-memory list.
Here is the modified version to allow a burst limit, by just checking if the length of the window is less than the max limit plus the burst allowance.
The bug in the seed code was that it didn't clean up old timestamps if a user stopped making requests, which causes a memory leak.
Yes, I can refactor it to be O(1) by using a leaky bucket algorithm instead.
